critical.issue: Cannot clear avatar_base64. update_profile builds update dict via {k: v for k, v in payload.model_dump().items() if v is not None}, so sending {avatar_base64: null} is stripped and the previous base64 string remains in MongoDB. Frontend removeAvatar() therefore appears to succeed but the avatar persists after re-fetch / next session. Fix suggestion: use payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) so explicit None values are persisted while truly omitted fields are skipped. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:262-269.

integration_issues.issue: Tied to backend bug above: tapping 'Remover foto' calls api.updateProfile({ avatar_base64: null }) and shows a success toast, but a subsequent GET /api/profile still returns the previous base64 string. rca_of_issue: Root cause: server.py:264 builds the update dict by filtering out all None values from ProfileUpdate.model_dump(). Pydantic v2 model_dump() returns None for every field the client didn't set (because they're declared Optional[...] = None). Without distinguishing 'omitted' from 'explicitly null', the only safe filter was to drop None — but that also drops legitimate clear-to-null requests. Fix: payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) — Pydantic tracks which fields were actually provided in the request body; combined with no `if v is not None` filter, this preserves null as a valid update. Reproduction: PUT /api/profile {avatar_base64:'data:...'} then PUT /api/profile {avatar_base64:null} then GET /api/profile -> still returns the original base64 string.
